title: Conversion of Oil-Containing Residue from Waste Oil Recycling Plant into Porous Carbon Materials by the Activation Method with Phosphoric Acid
content: In the waste oil recycling industry, large amounts of oil-containing sludge were still generated, thus posing a resource-depleted issue if it was disposed of or incinerated without energy recov-ery or residual oil utilization.  In this work, the chemical activation experiments by using phosphoric acid (H3PO4) were performed at a lower temperature (600°C) for holding 30 min to produce the porous carbon products.  From the results of the pore property analysis, it showed an increasing trend with impregnation ratio from 0.5 to 2.0.  Based on the Brunau-er–Emmett–Teller (BET) model, the maximal BET surface area was about 70 m2/g, which was indicative of the hysteresis loop and the type IV isotherms in the resulting carbon product.  In addition, the enhancement in the pore properties of carbon products by acid-washing was superior to those by water-washing and without post-washing.  By the observations of using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS), the carbon product featured its porous structure and inherent magnetism due to its richness of iron oxides.  In this regard, it can be used as an efficient adsorbents or catalyst supports due to its simple re-covery (or separation) if exhausted.
